rooms.4500: You step through a gap in the old garden wall, with the trade road behind you to the south, running back across the Great Field of Garathorm. The gravel path is split by shoots of knotweed and lined with flowers far too bright, red as fresh wounds and violet as bruises. The air is warm, heavy and sweet. Paths lead on north and east between the beds, and west toward the glint of a pond.
rooms.4501: Rose bushes the size of haystacks have swallowed this part of the garden, their thorns hooked and their blooms wet with a sticky dew. The path narrows to a single trampled line between them. It runs north toward the edge of a pond, east along more overgrown beds, and south back to the garden's entrance. Something rustles among the roses and then goes still.
rooms.4504: A round pond lies here, its surface so choked with lily pads and green scum that the water is almost invisible. Dragonflies as long as a hand hover and dart above it, and the reeds along the bank sway though no wind stirs. The path bends away north toward a great glasshouse, and south it returns to the tangled garden. The mud at the water's edge is printed with narrow, dragging marks.
rooms.4507: The greenhouse rises before you, a long hall of iron ribs and clouded glass, many panes cracked and furred with green. Its door hangs open on a single hinge, and warm wet air breathes out of it, thick with the smell of rot and honey. The path leads north through the doorway into the glasshouse, east along its outer wall, and south back to the pond. Pale tendrils have crept out through the broken panes and curl over the frame.
rooms.4524: Inside the glasshouse the heat presses on you like a damp hand. Rows of slatted benches run off into the green gloom, crowded with pots whose tenants have long since burst their clay and rooted into the floor. The doorway lies south, back to the garden, while the glass-roofed hall continues north, east and west between the benches. Water drips from the roof ribs, and every drop is tinted faintly green.
rooms.4527: This is the back of the greenhouse, where the benches give way to a bed of black soil, churned deep. Fat pitcher plants as tall as a man nod on thick stems, their hooded mouths brimming with a syrupy fluid that hums with drowning flies. Narrow aisles lead east and west along the glass, and south the way returns to the central aisle. The panes are so thick with moisture that nothing outside can be seen.
rooms.4528: In this corner of the glasshouse the iron frame is wrapped in a single huge vine, its trunk thick as a man's waist and its leaves slick as wet leather. Pale blossoms hang overhead, opening and closing slowly as if they were breathing. Dead moths lie scattered on the flagstones beneath them, dusted gold with pollen. The aisle runs south toward a door in the side wall, and west back along the rear of the hall.
rooms.4529: A glass door stands in the side wall of the greenhouse, its frame wedged open by a root as thick as a cable. Beyond it the outer path is bright with sunlight, a welcome relief from the oppressive heat. Spiny cacti and bloated succulents crowd the benches, bursting with swollen red fruit. The aisle continues north into the corner and west toward the middle of the hall, while the door leads east.
rooms.4510: A flagged path hugs the outer wall of the glasshouse, its stones heaved up by roots and fringed with pale moss. Condensation runs down the glass in long streaks, and shapes shift behind it in the green light. The path runs north and south along the wall, and a glass door to the west leads back into the greenhouse. A trellis of dead vines leans against the frame, its blossoms crumbling to brown dust.
rooms.4511: The path follows the glasshouse into a quieter, shadier stretch, where the glass is so stained with algae that the greenhouse shows only as a dark bulk. Foxgloves taller than a man crowd both sides, their speckled bells nodding together. A rusting watering can lies on its side at the verge. North the path opens onto bare ground, and south it follows the wall back around.
rooms.4516: A round clearing opens in the garden, its grass flattened as though by some great weight. A sundial stands in the middle, its bronze gnomon bent and its face blotched with lichen. Paving shows through the weeds to the north, where a plaza begins, and a heap of grey rock rises to the east. The path back along the glasshouse leads south.
rooms.4515: A paved plaza spreads out here, its flagstones cracked and lifted by weeds with pink flowers that glisten like raw meat. A dry fountain in the centre holds a stone nymph whose face has been eaten smooth by moss. Curved iron benches face a white pavilion, which stands to the north, while the clearing lies south and another stretch of the plaza west. Humidity beads on every surface.
rooms.4533: An octagonal pavilion of white painted wood stands here, its roof sagging under a mantle of climbing creeper. The floorboards are soft with damp and strewn with petals, and lanterns hang cold from the rafters, their glass fogged green. Tea tables are laid for guests who never came, the cups full of rainwater and drowned blossoms. The open sides give onto the plaza to the south and a lawn of low beds to the east.
rooms.4531: A garden of low box-edged beds stretches around you, the borders long since grown shaggy and spilled together. Snapdragons gape in rows, and bees as fat as thumbs drone drunkenly from flower to flower. Piled stones to the south mark the rockery, the pavilion's white roof shows to the west, and a shaded way leads north beneath old trees.
rooms.4532: Old yews and crooked apple trees meet overhead, making a green tunnel where the light falls in coins. The path underfoot is mossy and soft, and windfalls lie rotting in the grass, split open and sticky. A faint scent of lilies drifts from the east, where an ivy-draped archway opens into a hidden place. South the path returns to the beds.
rooms.4534: A walled garden, secret and silent, is closed in on all sides by high brick walls blanketed with ivy. At its heart a mad botanist's private work lies in neat, terrible rows: flowers with human-shaped buds, and a bed of pale bulbs that twitch in the soil. A cracked stone bench sits beside a basin of black water. The only way out is the archway to the west, through which the path under the trees can be seen.
rooms.4530: Heaps of weathered limestone have been piled into a rockery, each crevice stuffed with alpine flowers, stonecrop and trailing moss in too-vivid colours. Water seeps from the stones in a tiny stream that ends in a stagnant pool, ringed with bright orange fungi. Loose rubble makes the footing treacherous. Paths lead north to a garden of low beds and west into a clearing.
rooms.4513: This end of the plaza is overlooked by a tall wall of clipped yew, its face trimmed flat and dark as a cliff. Cracked tiles form a mosaic of a spreading flower, half of it hidden under creeping weeds. The plaza continues east, and a narrow gap in the hedge leads south into the labyrinth. A cold draught seeps out of that gap, smelling of earth and old leaves.
rooms.4517: Walls of dense, thorny hedge rise on every side, twice the height of a man and woven so tight that no light slips between the leaves. The gravel underfoot is dark and damp, strewn with snapped twigs. Branches stir softly in the corridors though the air is still. The only open way is the gap to the north, leading back to the plaza.
rooms.4512: The path swings round the corner of the glasshouse here, where the iron frame has rusted to the colour of dried blood. A rain barrel stands under a downpipe, brimming over with green water. Hyacinths and lilies crowd the verges in a heavy, sickly perfume. The path runs north along the wall, south to a garden of tangled beds, and west toward the greenhouse door.
rooms.4502: Four paths cross here amid overgrown flowerbeds, and a toppled stone urn lies in a drift of nettles. Giant sunflowers lean over the way, their dark faces turned to follow you. From this crossing the way leads north toward the glasshouse, west to the rose-choked beds, south to more garden, and east into a patch of wiry grass.
rooms.4506: A thick mat of crab grass has overrun the old lawn, its jointed stems creeping out in all directions and rooting at every node. The grass hums with a faint dry clicking, like claws on glass. A low wall of crumbling brick closes the field in, and a rusted croquet hoop leans in the tangle. The only path out leads west back to the garden.
rooms.4505: This corner of the garden was once a kitchen plot, and the ghosts of cabbages and onions still sprawl in the beds, grown to a monstrous size. A rotting scarecrow's post stands among them, its crossbar empty. Lettuce leaves as broad as shields tremble beside the path. The way runs north toward a crossing of paths, and west to the garden's entrance.
rooms.4526: This is a far corner of the glasshouse, where condensation hangs like rain and the panes glow with green fire. Orchids dangle from the rafters in dripping curtains, their lips red and wet and strangely toothed. A drain in the flagstones gurgles faintly. The aisle leads east along the rear wall and south along the side of the hall.
rooms.4525: A workbench runs along the glass here, scarred by knives and stained with sap in many colours. Broken seed trays and glass jars are heaped beneath it in a tangle of dust and webs. A hand-painted sign above the bench is blotted by mould. The aisle runs north into the corner and east to the centre of the greenhouse.
rooms.4503: The pond stretches out beside the path here, wide and brown, with a small island rising from its centre. Stepping stones, green with slime, make a crooked line through the shallows to the north. A willow trails its branches in the water, and the bank is churned by heavy, dragging marks. The path leads east to the garden's entrance and west along a winding way.
rooms.4508: The island is a small hump of black earth, crowned with one gnarled tree whose branches are hung with strings of pale, glistening seed pods. Reeds ring the shore, and the water laps at the roots in slow oily swells. A cracked statue of a stooped man lies half sunk in the mud. Stepping stones lead south to the near bank and north across the water to the far one.
rooms.4509: The path winds between hedges of box that have run wild, its gravel hidden under creeping moss. Passion flowers, bright as painted fans, hang from the branches in garlands. The ground squelches underfoot, and the scent of damp bark is strong. East the way runs back to the pond, and west it brings you to the foot of the glasshouse.
rooms.4518: Another passage between the high hedges, this one narrow enough that thorns catch at your sleeves on either side. The gravel is slick with a black ooze, and a trail of crushed leaves winds on and bends out of sight. Somewhere deeper in, the hedge creaks as though it were stretching.
rooms.4519: A small square in the maze, with a rotted wooden seat set into a niche cut in the hedge. The leaves overhead are woven so densely they make a green ceiling, and a damp gloom lies over everything. Tiny white flowers grow in the seat's cracks, sweet and sickly. Every gap leads into yet another wall of green.
rooms.4520: The hedges here have been clipped into the shapes of animals: a stag, a hound, a swan, each now overgrown into a shaggy parody. Moisture glitters on the leaves, and the gravel crunches loudly in the hush. A smell of crushed mint and something meatier hangs in the air. The topiary seems to lean closer whenever you look away.
rooms.4521: Roots as thick as ropes have lifted the gravel into ridges here, and the hedge walls bulge where the roots have grown through them. Black berries hang in clusters at head height, glossy and waxy. The light is a dim, underwater green. Scraps of torn cloth flutter from the thorns, a warning of what the hedge has taken.
rooms.4522: The passage opens into a wider walk, with an old stone lantern at the corner choked by ivy. Hedge walls stand on every side, tall and dark, and the earth underfoot is trampled hard. A glimmer of open ground shows through a gap at the far end, where the labyrinth thins out. The silence is thick enough to feel.
rooms.4523: The passage ends in a blank wall of ancient yew, hung with creepers that have twisted themselves into thick, writhing curtains. The ground is bare earth, dotted with rings of pale mushrooms. Overhead a patch of sky shows, grey and faintly humid. The only way back is west, along the labyrinth passage.

4516.description: The bronze gnomon is bent far out of true, and the hours around the dial are overgrown with lichen. Someone has scratched the words 'Nothing keeps time here' into the rim.

4515.description: The stone nymph holds an empty urn above a basin of dry leaves. Moss has crept over her features, so that she seems to wear a green mask.

4525.description: Beneath the mould, a few faded letters survive: 'Doctor I. Vane, Experimental Plantings. Do not water the specimens.'

4534.description: The basin is cut from a single block of dark stone, and the water in it never ripples. Stems of tiny white flowers stand up out of it, all leaning the same way.

creatures.long_desc: A giant garden spider hangs motionless in a web strung between two flowerbeds, its striped belly swollen.
creatures.description: The spider is as big as a hound, its legs banded yellow and black like a wasp's. Dewdrops cling to its web and every strand quivers as it turns to watch you.

creatures.long_desc: A snapping flytrap as tall as a man sways on its thick stem, its spiked jaws slowly opening.
creatures.description: Its two hinged leaves are fringed with white spines and lined in wet crimson. Bones and scraps of cloth lie in the soil about its root.

creatures.long_desc: A feral gardener in a tattered smock crouches among the flowers, muttering to the plants as he clips them.
creatures.description: Leaves and thorns are tangled in his beard, and his eyes shine with a tender madness. He clutches a long, crooked blade as if it were a child.

creatures.long_desc: A hulking hedge ogre, shaped of yew and bramble, stands very still among the leaves.
creatures.description: It is a giant figure of clipped hedge, with eyes of dark berries and hands like bundles of thorned branches. Gravel rolls from its shoulders as it breathes in the damp air.

creatures.long_desc: A huge marsh crocodile lies half submerged in the shallows, only its eyes and snout showing.
creatures.description: Its scaled back is crusted with mud and pond weed, and its jaws are crowded with yellow teeth. It was no doubt brought here as a curiosity and left to grow.

creatures.long_desc: Queen Bloom, a vast carnivorous flower, rises from the greenhouse floor on a nest of coiling vines.
creatures.description: Her petals are crimson and cream, each as big as a door, and a sweet drugging scent rolls off her in waves. In the dark heart of the bloom a wet mouth gapes, ringed with thorns.

creatures.short_desc: Doctor Ilmeric Vane, the Mad Botanist
creatures.long_desc: Doctor Ilmeric Vane, the Mad Botanist, bends over a bed of twitching bulbs, whispering to them.
creatures.description: He is a gaunt man in a stained green coat, his hands stained to the wrists with sap and his hair full of petals. His eyes are bright and fixed, and he smiles as though you were a seedling that has finally taken root.

items.room_desc: A curved sickle with a briar-wood handle lies here.
items.description: The blade is notched and stained green with old sap. The handle is a twist of living briar that still bears a few thorns.

items.short_desc: a pair of spider silk gloves
items.room_desc: A pair of spider silk gloves lies here.
items.description: The silk is pale and fine, strong enough to turn a knife yet soft against the skin.

items.room_desc: A pair of boots stitched from crocodile hide lies here.
items.description: The scaled leather is thick and waterproof, and smells faintly of the pond. The soles grip wet stone like claws.

items.room_desc: A crown of crimson petals, strangely fresh, lies here.
items.description: The petals are as thick as leather and never wilt. Warm scent drifts from the crown, and for a moment you feel the vines listening.

items.room_desc: A pair of long silver pruning shears lies here.
items.description: The blades are long, narrow and keen, and etched with tiny leaves. The handles are worn smooth by years of one man's hands.
